extra_vocab.zh: 平易近人的、容易親近的
extra_vocab.en: easy to talk to and friendly to other people
extra_vocab.note: 文中說話者用它形容自己友善、別人容易來搭話。後面接 but，表示「容易親近」不等於「外向」。

example.en: Everyone likes Ms. Chen because she is an approachable manager.
example.zh: 大家都喜歡陳小姐，因為她是個平易近人的主管。

example.en: The new staff members are friendly and approachable during training.
example.zh: 新進員工在訓練期間友善又容易親近。

example.en: Good leaders remain approachable even when the schedule is very busy.
example.zh: 好的領導者即使行程很滿，也保持平易近人。

examples.en: Our manager is very approachable, so staff often ask her for advice.
examples.zh: 我們的經理非常平易近人，所以員工常向她請教。

examples.en: Customers like the approachable service team at our front desk.
examples.zh: 客人喜歡我們櫃台那個容易親近的服務團隊。

examples.en: The company wants an approachable leader who listens to the team.
examples.zh: 公司想找一位願意傾聽團隊、容易親近的領導者。

confusable.diff: reachable 指「能被聯絡到」；approachable 指個性好相處、容易接近。

example.en: Please stay reachable by phone while you travel this week.
example.zh: 本週你出差時，請保持電話能聯絡得到。

confusable.diff: available 指「有空、可取得」；approachable 指人的個性。

example.en: Mr. Lin is available for a short meeting at three.
example.zh: 林先生三點有空開一個短會。

similar.diff: friendly 是一般的友善；approachable 強調別人敢主動來找他說話。

example.en: The friendly receptionist welcomed every guest at the door.
example.zh: 友善的櫃台人員在門口歡迎每一位賓客。

example.en: Our sales team is friendly with every new customer.
example.zh: 我們的業務團隊對每位新客戶都很友善。

example.en: The helpful clerk showed us where the printers are.
example.zh: 那位樂於幫忙的店員告訴我們印表機在哪裡。

example.en: Please be polite when you answer calls from customers.
example.zh: 接聽客戶來電時請保持禮貌。

example.en: We should approach the client with a clear offer.
example.zh: 我們應該帶著明確的提案去找客戶。

derived.link: approachable 去掉 -able 加 -ability，變成名詞，像 availability

example.en: A leader’s approachability helps staff share problems early.
example.zh: 領導者的平易近人讓員工能及早說出問題。

derived.link: un- 表示「不」，加在 approachable 前，意思相反，像 unhappy

example.en: Some employees find the director unapproachable and rarely ask questions.
example.zh: 有些員工覺得主任難以親近，很少發問。

extra_vocab.en: friendly and enjoying meeting other people
extra_vocab.note: 文中用來描述愛社交、主動與人互動的個性。說話者否定自己「特別外向」，表示自己喜歡與人相處，但不愛當焦點。

example.en: Her outgoing personality helps her work well with customers.
example.zh: 她外向的個性讓她和客戶合作得很好。

example.en: Our receptionist is outgoing and friendly with every visitor.
example.zh: 我們的接待人員對每位訪客都外向又友善。

example.en: Outgoing calls from this phone are recorded for quality control.
example.zh: 這支電話撥出的通話會被錄音以控管品質。

examples.en: Maria is outgoing, so she easily makes friends at company events.
examples.zh: 瑪莉亞很外向，所以在公司活動中很容易交到朋友。

examples.en: We need an outgoing sales rep who enjoys meeting new clients.
examples.zh: 我們需要一位喜歡認識新客戶的外向業務代表。

examples.en: Please put the outgoing mail in the box by noon.
examples.zh: 請在中午前把要寄出的郵件放進箱子。

examples.en: The outgoing manager will train her replacement next week.
examples.zh: 即將離任的經理下週會訓練接任者。

confusable.diff: ongoing 指「持續進行中的」；outgoing 指個性外向，或「離開、發出的」。

example.en: The ongoing project will continue until the end of June.
example.zh: 這個進行中的專案會持續到六月底。

confusable.diff: incoming 是「進來的」，和 outgoing 的「發出的」意思相反。

example.en: The incoming manager will start work on Monday morning.
example.zh: 即將上任的經理星期一早上開始上班。

confusable.diff: shy 指「害羞」，是 outgoing 在個性上的反義字。

example.en: The shy intern rarely speaks during the weekly meeting.
example.zh: 那位害羞的實習生在每週會議中很少發言。

similar.diff: sociable 強調喜歡和人往來；outgoing 更強調主動、有活力。

example.en: He is sociable and often joins the team for lunch.
example.zh: 他很善於交際，常和團隊一起吃午餐。

similar.diff: talkative 只是「話多」；outgoing 是整體個性外向。

example.en: The talkative guest kept asking questions about the schedule.
example.zh: 那位話很多的賓客一直詢問行程的問題。

example.en: The friendly guide answered all questions about the hotel.
example.zh: 那位友善的導遊回答了所有關於飯店的問題。

example.en: She felt confident when she gave the sales report.
example.zh: 她做業績報告時覺得很有自信。

senses.en: friendly and enjoying meeting other people

example.en: He is outgoing and speaks easily with strangers at trade shows.
example.zh: 他個性外向，在商展上很容易和陌生人交談。

senses.en: leaving a job or position soon
senses.distinguish: 後面接 manager、director 等職稱，指即將離職的人。

example.en: The outgoing director introduced her successor at the meeting.
example.zh: 即將卸任的主任在會議上介紹了她的接任者。

senses.distinguish: 搭配 mail、calls、emails 等物品，指往外發出。

example.en: All outgoing emails must include the company logo.
example.zh: 所有寄出的電子郵件都必須附上公司標誌。

extra_vocab.en: to start something or make it begin
extra_vocab.note: 文中指「主動開啟對話」。說話者喜歡社交，但通常等別人先開口，所以不太會主動發起交談。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: initiate 是及物動詞，後面直接接受詞，如 initiate a conversation，不要寫成 initiate to。

example.en: Mr. Wong initiates most of the discussions in our weekly meeting.
example.zh: 王先生在我們的週會中發起大部分的討論。

example.en: The bank initiated the transfer on Monday morning.
example.zh: 銀行在星期一早上啟動了這筆轉帳。

example.en: She is initiating a new training plan for the sales team.
example.zh: 她正在為業務團隊發起一項新的訓練計畫。

example.en: It takes courage to initiate a conversation with a senior manager.
example.zh: 要和資深經理主動攀談需要勇氣。

example.en: Please initiate contact with the supplier before Friday.
example.zh: 請在星期五前主動聯絡供應商。

example.en: Our department plans to initiate a project to reduce waste.
example.zh: 我們部門計畫啟動一個減少浪費的專案。

examples.en: The committee will initiate the changes after the budget is approved.
examples.zh: 預算通過後，委員會將開始推動這些改變。

examples.en: Customers can initiate a refund request on our website.
examples.zh: 客戶可以在我們的網站上發起退款申請。

examples.en: HR will initiate the hiring process next Monday.
examples.zh: 人資部門下星期一將啟動招聘流程。

confusable.diff: imitate 是「模仿」；initiate 是「發起、開始」。

example.en: Interns often imitate the way senior staff talk to clients.
example.zh: 實習生常模仿資深員工和客戶說話的方式。

confusable.diff: terminate 是「終止」，和 initiate 的「開始」意思相反。

example.en: The company may terminate the contract with thirty days’ notice.
example.zh: 公司可在三十天前通知後終止合約。

similar.diff: start 最常用、語氣一般；initiate 較正式，強調是由某人發起。

example.en: Let’s start the meeting now because everyone has arrived.
example.zh: 大家都到了，我們現在開會吧。

similar.diff: kick off 較口語，常用於活動、專案或會議的開場。

example.en: We will kick off the campaign with a short meeting.
example.zh: 我們會以一場簡短的會議來開始這次活動。

example.en: The training session will begin at nine o’clock tomorrow.
example.zh: 訓練課程明天九點開始。

example.en: The company will launch a new app next month.
example.zh: 公司下個月將推出一款新的應用程式。

example.en: I would like to propose a change to the schedule.
example.zh: 我想提議更改時程。

derived.link: initiate 的詞幹加 -al，變成形容詞，「一開始的」

example.en: The initial cost of the system was higher than expected.
example.zh: 這套系統的初期費用比預期高。

example.en: Initially, the plan looked simple, but it became complicated.
example.zh: 起初這個計畫看起來很簡單，後來變複雜了。

derived.link: initiate 的詞幹加 -ive，指主動開始做事的能力

example.en: Thank you for taking the initiative to organize the event.
example.zh: 謝謝你主動籌辦這場活動。

example.en: The initiation of the project was delayed by a month.
example.zh: 專案的啟動延後了一個月。

extra_vocab.en: to give something, such as ideas or help, to a group
extra_vocab.note: 文中指「有想法可以提供時才開口分享」，說話者不會為了說話而說話。這裡的受詞是 something，也就是有價值的意見。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: contribute to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接名詞或 V-ing，不接原形動詞；也可直接接受詞，如 contribute ideas。

example.en: Good teamwork contributes to the success of every project.
example.zh: 良好的團隊合作對每個專案的成功都有貢獻。

example.en: Mr. Lee contributed several useful ideas to the proposal.
example.zh: 李先生為這份提案提供了幾個有用的想法。

example.en: Ms. Park is contributing a short article to the newsletter.
example.zh: 朴小姐正為通訊刊物撰寫一篇短文。

example.en: Please contribute ideas for the new product before Friday.
example.zh: 請在星期五前為新產品提供想法。

example.en: New staff should feel free to contribute to a discussion.
example.zh: 新進員工可以放心參與討論並發表意見。

example.en: Each member must contribute to the project every week.
example.zh: 每位成員每週都必須為專案出一份力。

examples.en: Everyone is welcome to contribute ideas during the planning meeting.
examples.zh: 歡迎大家在規劃會議中提供想法。

examples.en: Our staff contribute part of their salary to the charity fund.
examples.zh: 我們的員工把部分薪水捐給慈善基金。

examples.en: Heavy traffic contributed to the delay in our delivery.
examples.zh: 塞車是我們送貨延誤的原因之一。

confusable.diff: distribute 是「分發、配送」；contribute 是「貢獻、捐出」。

example.en: We will distribute the new brochures at the trade show.
example.zh: 我們會在商展上發放新的簡介手冊。

confusable.diff: attribute 當動詞是「把…歸因於」，常寫成 attribute A to B。
confusable.usage: attribute 當名詞時重音在前（/ˈætrəbjut/），意思是「特質」；當動詞時重音在後。

example.en: Experts attribute the sales drop to higher prices.
example.zh: 專家把銷售下滑歸因於價格變高。

confusable.diff: donate 專指無償捐出錢或物品；contribute 範圍更廣，也可指意見與努力。

example.en: Several companies donated computers to the local school.
example.zh: 幾家公司把電腦捐給當地學校。

similar.diff: chip in 較口語，常指大家一起出錢或出力。

example.en: Everyone can chip in a few dollars for the gift.
example.zh: 大家可以各出幾塊錢買禮物。

similar.diff: offer 是「提供」，強調主動表示願意給；contribute 強調成為整體的一部分。

example.en: Feel free to offer suggestions at any time.
example.zh: 隨時歡迎提出建議。

example.en: Our company will donate books to the community library.
example.zh: 我們公司將捐書給社區圖書館。

example.en: The hotel provides free breakfast for all guests.
example.zh: 飯店為所有房客提供免費早餐。

example.en: Please share the report with the whole team today.
example.zh: 請今天把報告分享給整個團隊。

example.en: Her contribution to the team was recognized at the annual dinner.
example.zh: 她對團隊的貢獻在年度晚宴上受到肯定。

example.en: He is a regular contributor to the company newsletter.
example.zh: 他是公司通訊刊物的固定投稿人。

senses.en: to give ideas or help to a group

example.en: Anyone who wants to contribute can speak after the presentation.
example.zh: 想發表意見的人可以在簡報後發言。

senses.en: to give money to help a person or group
senses.distinguish: 後面接金額或 money，常和 to + 機構一起出現。

example.en: The firm will contribute 5,000 dollars to the school.
example.zh: 這家公司將捐五千美元給學校。

senses.en: to be one reason why something happens
senses.distinguish: 固定用 contribute to + 結果，主詞常是原因或事件。

example.en: Poor planning contributed to the late delivery of the order.
example.zh: 規劃不佳是訂單延遲送達的原因之一。

extra_vocab.en: able to do things without help from other people
extra_vocab.note: 文中指說話者能自己做決定、自己享受獨處，不需要靠別人或團體。語氣是正面的，帶有自在、自主的意思。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: independent 後面常接介系詞 of，例如 independent of the company；名詞是 independence，不要寫成 independency。

example.en: The company hired an independent contractor to design the website.
example.zh: 公司聘請了一位獨立承包商來設計網站。

example.en: The review team works independent of the sales department.
example.zh: 審查小組獨立於業務部門運作。

example.en: We value independent thinkers who can solve problems alone.
example.zh: 我們重視能獨立解決問題的獨立思考者。

examples.en: We are looking for an independent worker who needs little supervision.
examples.zh: 我們正在找不需要太多監督的獨立工作者。

examples.en: An independent auditor will review our financial report.
examples.zh: 獨立的稽核人員將審查我們的財務報告。

examples.en: She became financially independent after getting a better job.
examples.zh: 她換到更好的工作後，在經濟上獨立了。

confusable.diff: dependent 指「依賴的」，和 independent 意思相反，後面接 on。
confusable.usage: dependent on 要用 on，independent 則常接 of。

example.en: The small shop is dependent on a few large customers.
example.zh: 這家小店依賴幾位大客戶。

confusable.diff: individual 指「個別的、單一的」；independent 指「不依賴他人的」。

example.en: Each individual employee must sign the safety form.
example.zh: 每位員工都必須簽署安全表格。

similar.diff: self-reliant 強調「靠自己」；independent 還可指不受他人控制。

example.en: Self-reliant staff can solve small problems without asking for help.
example.zh: 能靠自己的員工不需要求助就能解決小問題。

example.en: You are free to choose your own working hours.
example.zh: 你可以自由選擇自己的工作時間。

example.en: He is confident that he can finish the task alone.
example.zh: 他有自信可以獨自完成這項工作。

example.en: Mr. Kim is responsible for the monthly sales report.
example.zh: 金先生負責每月的業績報告。

derived.link: independent 去掉 in- 和 -ent，剩下詞幹 depend，意思是「依靠」

example.en: Our success will depend on good teamwork and clear goals.
example.zh: 我們的成功將取決於良好的團隊合作和明確的目標。

example.en: We need a dependable supplier who delivers on time.
example.zh: 我們需要一個準時交貨、可靠的供應商。

derived.link: independent 的 -ent 改成 -ence，變成名詞，像 difference

example.en: Financial independence gives her more freedom to change jobs.
example.zh: 財務獨立讓她更自由地轉換工作。

example.en: The two teams worked independently and shared results on Friday.
example.zh: 兩個團隊各自獨立作業，並在星期五分享成果。

senses.en: able to do things without help from others

example.en: Tom is independent and rarely asks for help with tasks.
example.zh: 湯姆很獨立，很少請人幫忙處理工作。

senses.en: not controlled by another company or group
senses.distinguish: 常修飾公司、機構、報告，如 independent audit，指不受他方影響。

example.en: The study was done by an independent research firm.
example.zh: 這項研究是由一家獨立的研究公司進行的。
